subject: Business
title: Selective Attention and Banner Blindness
description: A quick, practical guide to Selective Attention and Banner Blindness.

hook.text: Eye-tracking studies show people's gaze literally skips over banner ads. Their brains pretend ads don't exist.

buildup.text: Selective attention means our brains filter out irrelevant stimuli to focus on what matters.

discovery.text: After years of web browsing, people have trained themselves to ignore anything that looks like an advertisement.

twist.text: This is why native advertising works: it disguises commercial messages as editorial content.

climax.text: The ethical line is thin. Effective marketing uses context, not deception, to bypass filters.

punchline.text: If it looks like an ad, the brain deletes it before you even notice.

quiz.question: What is banner blindness?
options: Users unconsciously ignore anything that looks like a web advertisement
Banners that are too small to read

details.summary: Banner blindness is a form of selective attention where users unconsciously ignore page elements that resemble advertisements. Decades of web ad exposure have trained the brain to filter out banner-shaped content, making traditional display advertising increasingly ineffective for reaching
details.whyItMatters: Businesses spend billions on display advertising that users literally cannot see due to trained inattentional blindness. Understanding banner blindness drives investment toward native content, contextual placement, and other formats that bypass the
takeaways: Users unconsciously ignore content that looks like banner advertisements
Eye tracking studies show people literally do not see most display ads on pages
Native content and contextual advertising bypass trained banner blindness

faq.question: Why does banner blindness occur even with novel ad designs?
faq.answer: The brain learns heuristics for what constitutes an ad based on position, shape, and visual characteristics. Anything in typical ad placements or with ad-like formatting gets automatically filtered. Even novel designs trigger the filter if they occupy expected ad locations on a page.

faq.question: What advertising formats effectively avoid banner blindness?
faq.answer: Native advertising that matches the platform's content format. Influencer endorsements within organic feeds. Content marketing that provides genuine value. In-stream video ads that interrupt desired content. Interactive experiences that require engagement. Sponsored search results in context.
